text:
Sports Illustrated framed it as a rescue: "How Filip Forsberg Broke out of his Slump and Saved Nashville's Season." The Predators have since stretched their winning streak to seven, and Forsberg has 14 points in his last ten games, including both goals in the 3-0 win in Los Angeles. He has 22 points in 20 games and 49 shots on 20.45 minutes a night.

His own game holds up. Seven goals on 6.77 expected goals (the quality of his chances) says the finishing is honest, and his 14.3% shooting sits inside our talent range. The part to discount is around him: Nashville has scored 12.9 more goals than its chances deserve with Forsberg on the ice, and on-ice luck like that fades. At five-on-five the Predators get 49.5% of the expected goals with him out there, roughly even. Evolving-Hockey's view of last season is the flip side, 2.5 expected wins against 0.9 actual: the bounces owed him then. He has gone two games without a point, which after a run like this is nothing to read into.
headline: Filip Forsberg's revival: real volume, kind bounces
